dedupe_keys.name: basgoed basic strategic freight transport model of the netherlands

description: BasGoed (from 'basic' and 'goed', good) is the basic strategic freight transport model that the Dutch Ministry of Infrastructure and the Environment commissioned as the first step towards a modular, transparent set of freight policy instruments. Its distribution and modal split models are described in a 2011 European Transport Conference paper by Gerard de Jong (Significance), Arnaud Burgess and Robbert Versteegh (NEA), Lori Tavasszy (TNO and TU Delft), Michiel de Bok (Significance) and Nora Schmorak (the ministry). Coverage: the Netherlands, split into 40 NUTS3 regions, plus 29 zones in the rest of the world, with ten NSTR level 1 commodity groups; zonal tonnes generated and attracted come from the economy module of the earlier SMILE+ model, and new models distribute flows to origin-destination pairs and split them between road, rail and inland waterways, estimated on transport data, transport cost data and route data. Format and access: the paper in the TU Delft repository; the model is owned by Rijkswaterstaat. Licence and cost: the paper is free to read; model access is not described and is assumed to be on request. Caveats: 2011 description; later versions may differ. It can supply national freight flows by mode for network flow and capacity planning studies of Dutch corridors. It relates to the STRAM freight network design model and TRANS-TOOLS in the catalogue.
